question: Does the webhook delivery pass stay inside the run (or command) that scheduled it?
defect: The webhook pass is bounded per POST by the target timeout_ms but has NO pass budget: deliver_events + deliver_reorgs loop over up to --webhook-limit (default 500) rows synchronously inside the scheduler tick, so the run loop cannot check its deadline until the pass hands control back — the run pays backlog x per-POST cost past its --seconds. Every signature walk was deadline-bounded in PULS BD; the webhook pass was the one scheduler consumer left. `webhook push` is a DRAIN command: its wall clock is the delivery work it completed (G3), and a stalled endpoint stops it at the first row — that is not this defect.

faces.name: D1_the_webhook_pass_outlives_the_run_deadline_on_the_carrier_and_stays_in_budget_on_the_fixed_side
faces.detail: baseline overshoot 29s vs fixed overshoot 3s (honest tail = shutdown budget 6s + one in-flight POST 250ms + exit slack) at 250ms/POST on a 200-row backlog, --seconds 30, --webhook-every 5

faces.name: D2_the_overrun_scales_with_the_backlog_on_the_carrier_and_not_on_the_fixed_side
faces.detail: same 250ms/POST, 200 vs 50 rows: baseline overrun grows by 25s (queue expects 38s) — fixed grows by -2s (≤ honest tail 11s)

faces.name: G3_push_drains_every_planted_row_and_exits_zero
faces.detail: push wall 51s for 200 rows = 253ms/row at 250ms/POST (the work itself); bodies 200/200 + 50/50 (baseline 200/200), exit 0

faces.name: G4_the_budget_does_not_starve_delivery
faces.detail: daemon delivered: fixed 98, budget_stops=1, rows_owed=102 — baseline delivered 200 (carrier pays the whole queue)
